title: Prefetch hysteresis + fallback cost analysis
content:
Summary:

Short: ran a targeted sweep to understand hysteresis behavior between paged and flash attention paths when prefetch budget changes, and quantify the end-to-end cost/latency tradeoffs when falling back to quantized fused ops under KV-cache pressure. Goal is to decide whether to add an explicit hysteresis window in kernel-selector or to rely on current throughput smoothing heuristics.

Why this matters:
- Customers with mixed sequence-length workloads see intermittent tail spikes. We suspect these are correlated with aggressive prefetch that temporarily increases memory pressure and causes kernel switch + rebuffering.
- Current selector flips between paged/flash rapidly for certain seq distributions; each flip incurs warmup + extra memcpy and increases 95/99p latency.
- If fallback to quantized fused ops is cheaper (cost-per-token) but higher latency, rollout policies could prefer cost during non-SLO-critical routes. Need data to tune.

Hypotheses:
1) There exists a prefetch budget range where flash has throughput advantage, but if prefetch overshoots by >X MB the system flips to paged and triggers kernel-handoff cost that dominates.
2) A small hysteresis window (e.g., 10% seq-prefetch tolerance) will cut flip frequency by ~70% and reduce 99p by ~15–25% for mixed workloads.
3) Quantized fused-op fallback reduces GPU memory footprint and per-token cost but increases first-token latency; combining hysteresis + conservative fallback yields best cost-latency Pareto.

Experiment matrix (swept parameters):
- Model: 13B decoder-only (v2.1) / typical Redwood-verified profile
- HW: Ampere A40 / 80GB (test cluster set a3-testing-7)
- Batch sizes: [1, 4, 16]
- Sequence mixes: 
  * short-only (prompt 32, gen 32)
  * mixed (50% prompts 32/gen 64, 30% prompts 128/gen 256, 20% long 512/512)
  * long-heavy (predominantly 512+)
- Prefetch budget: [low, default, +25%, +50%, +100%] (concrete MB values recorded per run)
- KV-cache pressure: enabled/disabled (simulate high reuse vs cold starts)
- Kernel selector hysteresis: off | 5% | 10% | 20% (percent change in sequence-prefetch before flip)
- Fallback policy: none | quantized-fused | cpu-fallback (rare)

Metrics captured (per-run):
- p50/p95/p99 latency (token and request-level)
- tail flip count (number of kernel selector switches per 10k requests)
- extra memcpy bytes (MB) during run
- GPU memory high-water mark
- tokens/sec and cost-estimate ($/1M tokens using internal unit pricing)
- warmup penalty: measured as average latency for first N tokens after switch

Quick notes on methodology:
- Each sweep: 15-minute steady-state after warmup. 5 independent runs per cell.
- Use tracebench + internal op-injection to mark kernel switches. 
- Telemetry: insert sampling at selector decision point to log prefetch footprint and candidate kernels.
- Keep background cluster noise low (dedicated lanes).

Key raw observations (high level):
- Flip frequency correlates strongly with +50% prefetch runs on mixed workload: median flip count jumped 3x vs default prefetch.
- Each flip carries ~8–12ms extra latency for the immediate tokens after switch and increases p99 by 18–27ms depending on batch.
- Hysteresis 10% reduced flips by ~65% on mixed workload; reduced p99 by ~12ms absolute (~11% relative).
- Quantized-fused fallback reduced GPU high-water mark by ~15–20% in high-KV pressure runs and reduced per-token cost estimate by ~9% but increased initial token latency by ~6–15ms.
- Long-heavy workloads rarely flip; paged path dominates there regardless of prefetch.

Representative numbers (mixed workload, batch=4):
- default prefetch, no-hysteresis: p50=8.6ms, p95=24.1ms, p99=46.8ms, flips/10k=38, cost=0.82 units
- +50% prefetch, no-hysteresis: p50=9.1ms, p95=27.8ms, p99=73.2ms, flips/10k=112, cost=0.94 units
- +50% prefetch, 10% hysteresis: p50=9.0ms, p95=25.9ms, p99=61.4ms, flips/10k=38, cost=0.91 units
- +50% prefetch, quant-fused fallback: p50=10.6ms, p95=28.5ms, p99=66.0ms, flips/10k=28, cost=0.85 units

Interpretation / root causes:
- Aggressive prefetch increases transient memory pressure and shifts kernel-choice heuristics toward paged paths (more conservative memory footprint). The selector is very sensitive to short-timescale spikes because it reacts to instantaneous footprints without smoothing.
- Warmup for flash kernels includes allocation + data-layout prep and sometimes re-initialization of fused-op kernels; that contributes the immediate token latency penalty.
- Quantized fused-ops avoid some memcpy and reduce HWM but at cost of added compute per token + accuracy considerations. When KV-cache reuse is high, quant-fused wins cost-wise.

Actionable recommendations (short-term):
1) Implement a 10% hysteresis window in kernel-selector with decay time of 200ms (tunable). Rationale: large reduction in flip frequency with negligible cost increase.
2) Add a small exponential smoothing on prefetch footprint input to selector (alpha ~0.2, 50–200ms window) to damp microbursts.
3) Expose a route-level policy to prefer quantized-fused fallback for non-SLO routes (cheaper only when KV-cache reuse > 40% & predicted seq < 256).
4) Telemetry: add counter for memcpy MB and break down warmup time per kernel so we can monitor regressions post-change.

Actionable recommendations (longer-term/experimental):
- Explore asynchronous prefetch throttling: cap inflight prefetch size per-device and backpressure upstream to router when device nearing HWM.
- Micro-optim: reduce allocation churn in flash warmup path (reuse scratch buffers across close-by streams).
- Eval accuracy impact of quantized-fused on typical customer prompts before wide rollout.

Open questions & experiments to run next:
- How does hysteresis interact with autoscaling burst policies? If we delay flips, do we create more sustained flash pressure that triggers node-level OOMs in worst-case? Need a safety test with synthetic spike sequences.
- Can we detect candidate flips earlier by looking at sequence-mix distribution at router and preemptively choose kernel? (move decision earlier in pipeline)
- What's the accuracy delta for quant-fused on safety-sensitive prompts? Work with evals team to run A/B.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Push small PR adding hysteresis parameter to selector (bench locally, add flag). Reference PR: git.redwood/corp/serving-runtime/pulls/423 (linked above).
- Add telemetry counters in selector: memcpy_mb, warmup_ms, selector_state_deltas.
- Create a dashboard tile for flips/10k and memcpy_mb high-water.
- Schedule a follow-up sync with Marco + Bench team to run autoscale-safety test.

Command snippets / repro pointers:
- run harness: ./bench/run_sequence_mix.sh --model=13b-v2 --batch=4 --mix=mixed --prefetch-mult=1.5 --kv-pressure=on --duration=900
- trace injection: tools/trace_injector --tag=selector --sample-rate=100 --out=traces/prefetch-50p.json
- compute cost: tools/cost_estimator --trace traces/prefetch-50p.json --pricing-file conf/pricing/2024-q4.json

Concluding note:
This is a working note. Results are noisy for small batch sizes; next runs should prioritize batch=4 as p95/p99 are most sensitive there for our typical PLG customers. If we get alignment on hysteresis + smoothing I can prototype PR and run a canary on staging lanes next week.

Signed: Priya Nair
